pr_title: i2c: bitbang: fix SDA pin configuration
pr_body:
The driver must be able to read from this pin as well as write to it.

Fixes #27855.
pr_comments: File this under "how did this ever work?".

issue_context.title: i2c bitbanging on nrf52840
comments: @pabigot Thanks for the answer. I am trying to use the bit-bang I2C driver. Is there any reason why I need to disable the existing driver? Could both the drivers not work simultaneously? What are the limitations? Is there something I can do to make them work simultaneously? I need an extra I2C driver at low frequencies. So I was planning on using bit-banged I2C driver.

If the TWI driver is active it controls the pins, so attempts to use the bitbang code will not work.  The devices aren't designed to be turned on and off, transferring control from one driver instance to another..  Your best option is to use two different sets of pins, one for the I2C and another for the bitbang.  Alternatively if the slow I2C devices would work at 100 kHz then use that (slowest) I2C speed with the TWI driver.

@pabigot Sorry, I should have probably mentioned that I was using different pins for different drivers (I2C-TWIM and GPIO-I2C). The issue seems to be something else for me. Any idea what else might be causing the trouble? Thanks.
Yes: the pins in the devicetree fragment you gave are the same pins normally used by the `i2c0` device.  Did you try adding the fragment I suggested?

@pabigot Yes, I have disabled i2c0. And also, the board I am using is custom, so i2c0 dts has different sda and scl pins assigned than the one mentioned above. Just in case, I have still disabled the i2c0 as you suggested. I still have the same issue. The i2c reads all '0' on the bus.
Ok, I can reproduce this.  Looks like the GPIO driver doesn't work on nrf52840.  Oddly, the line signals are good, so it's something in the API.  I'll look into it.

@pabigot  Wow. This worked -> #27875 . I wonder why? Maybe it has something to do with the behavior in nrf52840 GPIO controller, since SDA needs to be bidirectional? Anyways, Thanks a lot for this patch. :)
@sviraaj I'm trying to use the gpio-i2c too but I can't seem to get the binding from the call to device_get_binding.  How are you getting it?  By calling device_get_binding("GPIO_I2C_0"); ??

Hi,
Yes, device_get_binding("GPIO_I2C_0")  will work. Make sure that you are
enabling it in prj.conf by setting CONFIG_I2C_GPIO=y and the corresponding
node in the device tree.

review_comments:
I suspect this will render the I2C GPIO bit banging driver useless on many GPIO controllers, since they fail configuration if both GPIO_INPUT and GPIO_OUTPUT are specified.

I tested the existing implementation on the FRDM-K64F using `PORT_PCR_ODE_MASK` pinmux configuration, which puts the given pin in open-drain mode. It's configured as an output, but the open drain configuration allows it to be pulled down - and that real value is read back.

One could argue, that the GPIO controller driver should allow GPIO_INPUT | GPIO_OUTPUT when the pin is configured as open-drain, but the GPIO controller driver has no easy way of knowing the pinmux configuration.
I've updated this so if configuring bidirectional fails it should fall back to the old way.
